structure: Part 5 read lines 7054 to 10530 of repos/trade-imports-stub/src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json in full: country records 167 to 250 of the 250-record JSON array, in file order (ascending MDM id, not by name), from Timor-Leste (line 7054) to Austria (line 10480), and the array's closing bracket at line 10530. Each record is about 40 lines (50 with blocks, more with a subdivision): id and countryUUID objects, ISONumeric, alpha2 and alpha3 objects each with value and ISO list metadata, independent, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, effectiveAlias, effectiveAlpha2, effectiveAlpha3, subDivisions and blocks. It covered all 84 records, one claim each with every field the scope names (claims 001 to 084, numbered record minus 166); the two subdivisions (GB-NIR on the GB record and ES-CN Canary Islands on Spain) with their ids, codes, names, categories and blocs; and every block membership country by country (GBNAG_SPS_EX on Lithuania, Bulgaria, Liechtenstein, the United Kingdom, Spain, Sweden, Slovenia and Austria, plus the unnamed block entries they carry). It also records what the slice shows across records: no system aliases, no independent true and four records without the key, the GB record with no effectiveAlias, the Canary Islands both as a country and as Spain's subdivision with a null ISONumeric, the ISO list metadata, the unpadded numeric codes, the ISO-style display names, and the id ordering.

The United Kingdom record (alpha2 GB, alpha3 GBR, ISONumeric 826) has no effectiveAlias key, so the stub serves no display name for the United Kingdom.
claims.note: The key is missing, not null: the line after systemAlpha3 is effectiveAlpha2. A consumer that labels a country by effectiveAlias gets nothing for GB. It is the only record in this part without an effectiveAlias.

claims.statement: The United Kingdom record carries one subdivision, Northern Ireland's ISO 3166-2 code GB-NIR, with subdivision id 19970d1f-c248-492e-b714-cefc3951934e (schemeId MDM-COUNTRY-SUBDIVISION, agency DEFRA) and code list ISO-3166-2, agency ISO, version 2024-06.
The GB-NIR subdivision has no name field, unlike Spain's ES-CN subdivision, which is named "Canary Islands"; the stub serves no display name for Northern Ireland.
claims.note: The code object is followed directly by countryCategory with no name key in between.

claims.statement: The GB-NIR subdivision has countryCategory categoryID 405.
The GB-NIR subdivision belongs to two blocs, EU_SPS_ALIGNED and GBNAG_SPS_EX, listed in a field spelt "blocs" (not "blocks" as at record level).
The United Kingdom record is a member of the GBNAG_SPS_EX block with includeCountry false, so the block takes in part of the UK (its subdivision) but not the country itself.
claims.note: That includeCountry false means only the subdivisions are in the block is read from the field name and from GB-NIR's own GBNAG_SPS_EX bloc; the file does not say what includeCountry means. It is the only GBNAG_SPS_EX membership in this part with includeCountry false.

claims.statement: The United Kingdom record's first block entry has no name, includeCountry false and an empty tags list.
claims.note: An unnamed block entry cannot be matched by a blocks filter on name; whether it stands for a block whose name was stripped from the saved response is not said.

The ES-CN Canary Islands subdivision has countryCategory categoryID 101.
The ES-CN Canary Islands subdivision belongs to two blocs, OMR and GBNAG_SPS_EX.
Spain's record is a member of the GBNAG_SPS_EX block with includeCountry true.

Spain's record has three block entries, where every other block-carrying record in this part has two: the first has only an empty tags list (no name and no includeCountry), the second is GBNAG_SPS_EX and the third has no name, includeCountry true and empty tags.
claims.note: The first entry is the only block entry in this part with no includeCountry key.

Only two records in this part carry a subdivision: the United Kingdom (GB-NIR) and Spain (ES-CN Canary Islands). The other 82 carry an empty subDivisions list.
No record in this part carries a system alias: systemAlias, systemAlpha2 and systemAlpha3 are null on all 84 records.
Every record in this part has system "gbnag", an id of the form gbnag-<uuid> with schemeId MDM-COUNTRY and schemeAgencyId DEFRA, and a countryUUID holding the same uuid without the gbnag- prefix.
claims.note: Checked with jq over all 84 records.

claims.statement: No record in this part is marked independent true: 80 records have "independent": false and four (Peru, Iraq, Mali and Fiji) have no independent key, so the flag does not tell sovereign states from territories in the stub's data.
claims.note: The counts are verbatim; that the flag cannot tell states from territories is inferred because states such as Austria and territories such as Bouvet Island both carry false.

claims.statement: The list mixes sovereign states with dependent territories and uninhabited areas, each as an ordinary country record: in this part Svalbard and Jan Mayen, Norfolk Island, Bouvet Island, Wallis and Futuna, Virgin Islands (U.S.), Bermuda, Heard Island and McDonald Islands, Mayotte, Curacao, Montserrat, Anguilla, Canary Islands, Antarctica, Northern Mariana Islands (the), Falkland Islands (the) [Malvinas], French Polynesia, Western Sahara*, Niue and Tokelau.
claims.note: Which entries are territories rather than states is general knowledge, not something the file marks.

claims.statement: The Canary Islands appear twice: as a country record of their own (IC, ICX, ISONumeric null, no blocks) and as Spain's subdivision ES-CN, which is in the GBNAG_SPS_EX bloc.
claims.note: Ambiguity, not reconciled: a country list built from effectiveAlias offers Canary Islands as a country outside GBNAG_SPS_EX, while the same place is inside it as part of Spain.

claims.statement: The Canary Islands record's ISONumeric is null rather than an object with a value, the only record in this part without a numeric code.

Every ISONumeric, alpha2 and alpha3 object in this part names listId ISO-3166-3, listAgencyId ISO and listVersionId 2024-06, ISONumeric included, though alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes are ISO 3166-1 codes.
claims.note: That the codes are ISO 3166-1 rather than 3166-3 is general knowledge; recorded as the file states it.

claims.statement: ISONumeric values are strings without leading zeros, so codes under 100 are one or two digits, such as Azerbaijan "31", Antarctica "10", Austria "40" and Australia "36".
On every record in this part effectiveAlpha2 and effectiveAlpha3 equal the record's own alpha2 and alpha3 values.
claims.note: Checked with jq over all 84 records. With no system alias on any record, the effective codes are the ISO codes.
